summary: Variance decomposition (linear model, 500K grid cells): cloud properties (area+tau) explain R²=0.439 of albedo variance, while geometric/invariant features (lat, lon, month) explain only R²=0.002. Unique cloud contribution: 44.7%; unique invariant: 1.1%. Results are stable across 2000-2012 and 2013-2025 subsets (R² within 0.004). INTERPRETATION: This tests a simplified form of H002 and finds that clouds (variable) dominate spatial albedo variance, not invariant geometry. HOWEVER this does not directly test H002's core claim — H002 predicts that fundamental physical constants (water optical properties, geometry) constrain the GLOBAL MEAN (~29%), not that they dominate spatial variance. A linear regression on spatial patterns cannot test this. H002's prediction requires global-mean analysis or analytical derivation from physical constants. This result is inconclusive for H002's actual claim, but confirms H001's relevance (clouds are the dominant variable factor).
